summary: British abolitionists Granville Sharp, Olaudah Equiano and Thomas Clarkson, galvanised by the 1781 Zong massacre, built the campaign that ended Britain's Atlantic slave trade with the 1807 Abolition Act.

evidence.note: Elmina fort on the Gold Coast converted into slave dungeons; model for later trading posts
account of the Elmina governor selecting and raping captive women
long segment on failed slaver Robert Stubbs leading into the Zong voyage
Zong reaches Jamaica in December 1781 after captives were thrown overboard
Equiano born around 1745 in Igbo country, modern Nigeria
Sharp meets the beaten enslaved youth Jonathan Strong in 1765, his first case
Sharp takes up the Zong case after Equiano alerts him; 1783 rehearing
Clarkson born 1760; 1785 Cambridge essay contest turns him to abolition
extended biography of John Newton, born 1725, slaver turned abolitionist clergyman
abolitionist publicity: Wedgwood seal, Brookes ship diagram posters, sugar boycott
Parliament passes the act abolishing the British slave trade in 1807
1840 World Anti-Slavery Convention and Clarkson's final years

notes: Primary is the trio named in the descriptions; Wilberforce is explicitly not covered in depth, so keyword only. Part 1 opens with ~30 min on the trade's history from 1471 (Portuguese in Ghana, 1518 start); treated as general background, so covered_span starts at Newton's birth. A reviewer may prefer adding the Atlantic slave trade as a subject and starting at 1471. Death years for Equiano and Clarkson from general knowledge. genocide-mass-killing reflects the Zong mass murder.
